message.reasoning:
We need to generate JUnit 4 test cases comprehensively testing all methods in Tokeniser. Provide a test class file with tests covering:

- constructor? can't directly instantiate because Tokeniser requires CharacterReader and ParseErrorList. Need to use real implementations from jsoup. Probably we can create a CharacterReader via new CharacterReader(String). That's part of jsoup parser. ParseErrorList can be created via ParseErrorList.tracking(int). Provide small errors list.

We need to test:

- read() behavior for character token emission vs non-char tokens. Hard to simulate all states. Might test simple use of emit(String) and read.

- emit methods: token, string, char[], int[], char.

- getState, transition, advanceTransition.

- consumeCharacterReference: test numeric and named references, hex, missing semicolon, invalid, replacement char, etc.

- createTagPending, emitTagPending, createCommentPending, emitCommentPending, createDoctypePending, emitDoctypePending.

- createTempBuffer, isAppropriateEndTagToken, appropriateEndTagName.

- error methods: error(state), eofError(state), characterReferenceError internal (via consumeCharacterReference), error(String). Validate that errors are added.

- currentNodeInHtmlNS returns true.

- unescapeEntities.

We need to be comprehensive but not exhaustive due to time. Provide tests that cover each branch.

Will need to import jsoup classes. The test class path: org.jsoup.parser.TokeniserTest.

Will use Tokeniser's package same as class.

Implementation details:

- CharacterReader: jsoup's class has constructor CharacterReader(String). Use that.

- ParseErrorList: static ParseErrorList.tracking(int maxErrors). Use that.

- For testing read() with character tokens: we can set up a Tokeniser with a custom state that will emit a token. However state is internal. Simpler: use emit(String) then call read() expecting a Character token with data.

But read() will loop while !isEmitPending, calling state.read(this, reader). Default state is Data, which will read characters and eventually set charsString? In Data state, it will read characters until a token is needed. Might be complex.

Simpler: directly test emit(String) and read() returning char token. Use Tokeniser.emit(String) then call read() and verify token type Character and data.

But read() will first while (!isEmitPending) state.read(this, reader). Since isEmitPending is false, it will call state.read which may consume from reader and maybe not set isEmitPending. However we have not added any characters to reader; we can give empty reader. Then state.read will likely set isEmitPending? Not sure.

Alternative: Use emit(String) then call read() after calling emit(String) and then manually set isEmitPending? Actually emit(String) does not set isEmitPending. It buffers chars. read() will loop while !isEmitPending; state.read will read from reader and may eventually set isEmitPending when encountering token. If we have empty reader, state.read may call error? Might loop infinitely? Not good.

Better approach: Use public methods to test logic without relying on read's state machine: test emit(Token) and verify that after calling emit(token) the internal fields reflect pending. However emit is void and sets isEmitPending true. We can then call read() and expect the token returned. So we can construct a Token (e.g., new Token.Comment()) and call tokeniser.emit(token). Then call tokeniser.read() expecting same token. Need to ensure read() does not attempt to consume chars. Since isEmitPending true, while loop will skip (condition is while (!isEmitPending) - it's false). Then it will go to else branch: charsBuilder length 0, charsString null, then isEmitPending false and return emitPending. Good. So test that.

Similarly test emit(String) and read() returns char token.

Also test emit(char) etc.

Test transition and getState.

Test advanceTransition: need to ensure reader.advance() moves position; we can verify reader's pos changes.

Test consumeCharacterReference:

- Numeric decimal reference: e.g., "&"? No numeric: "A" should return codepoint 65 'A'. Provide reader with "A" then call tokeniser.consumeCharacterReference(null,false). Should return int[]{65}. Also test missing semicolon: "&#65" no semicolon; should still return 65? According to code: if !matchConsume(";") characterReferenceError("missing semicolon") but still returns codepoint after parsing. So we can test that errors list contains error.

- Hex numeric: "A" returns 65.

- Invalid numeric >0x10FFFF leads to replacement char.

- Named entity: "amp;"? Actually named without '&' because method assumes already after '&' consumed? In consumeCharacterReference, it reads from current reader position after '&' has been consumed? In unescapeEntities they call consumeCharacterReference after consuming '&'. So for testing we should set reader to "amp;" maybe? The method will match letter then digit sequence, then look for ';' etc. Provide "amp;" expecting codepoint for '&' (38). Entities.codepointsForName("amp") returns 38.

- Test attribute context: if after named entity there is a letter etc, should reject.

- Test that when additionalAllowedCharacter provided and matches next char, returns null.

Test isAppropriateEndTagToken:

- Create tokeniser, set lastStartTag via emitting a start tag token. Use tokeniser.createTagPending(true) to get a start tag, set its name, then emitTagPending to set lastStartTag. Then create end tag pending with same name and test isAppropriateEndTagToken true. Also false case.

Test appropriateEndTagName returns lastStartTag.

Test createTagPending returns same object and resets.

Test createCommentPending and emitCommentPending: after creating comment pending, set data, emit, read token.

Simplify: after creating comment pending, set commentPending.data("test")? Need to look at Token.Comment class (not provided). Might be more complex.

Given time, we can limit to methods we can easily test without deep internal token classes.

We can still test createDoctypePending and emitDoctypePending similar to comment.

But we can at least test that after calling createDoctypePending, doctypePending is reset (maybe name null). Not needed.

Focus on methods with observable behavior: getState, transition, advanceTransition, consumeCharacterReference, isAppropriateEndTagToken, appropriateEndTagName, error handling (error(String)), unescapeEntities.

Implement tests.

We'll need to import jsoup classes. Ensure test compiled.

Write test class TokeniserTest with @Test methods.

Edge Cases: For error tests, after calling tokeniser.error(state) we verify errors.size() increased.

Implementation details for ParseErrorList: ParseErrorList errors = ParseErrorList.tracking(10).

Now produce final output with markers.
